scenario: AITA for refusing an additional guest at our wedding | Thanks for watching this post. First time writing here and non-native English speaker. I am getting married very soon. As you can imagine, this takes a lot of preparation. I'm talking here about the civil wedding, which will be very intimate and consequently restricted to our very close family: parents, siblings and, in my case, godparents and their children. The wedding will happen in another country, so this takes a lot of preparation as it is in another culture. When I made the invitations, I've been clear: I invited my parents (2 p.) and my godparents' family (4 p.). I've been very flexible, I told everyone that they could join us anytime they like (i.e., arrive in the country when they wish because I understand it's complicated when you have 4 different jobs etc) as long as they'll be present for the ceremony. Moreover, because the destination is far, my in-laws kindly proposed to offer the accommodation to all of them. The wedding is now in one month and I just received a message from my godmother saying that they have booked the flights, and they will be 5 because the gf of my cousin is joining. That's where I am really feeling uncomfortable: I receive this as a 'fait accompli' (done deal) without any prior consultation, without even asking me if that's ok to have an additional person (that I've never met). I've always been clear about the number of people invited. I just can't stand to receive this kind of 'news' via a late evening text message. It's not that I'm against that additional person. It's just the way that I'm put in front of this, as if I had nothing to say. And we're not talking about the 'party' wedding, but something very special that is meant to be in strict intimacy. Moreover, I know that they have their tickets since 1 month, and I was waiting for their news to plan the trip etc. So they literally waited 1 month to announce it, now that the date is getting closer. I just don't understand this kind of behavior. It costs nothing to make a quick phone call before booking anything, and to ask if it's possible, etc. In sum, they just invited someone at my wedding, someone that wasn't ever planned and that I don't even know. This morning, I sent a polite message saying: 'I'm confused by your news, I've always been clear about the number of guests and why I picked these specific guests (i.e. you) for our wedding. Why haven't you called me and asked me before booking anything? I'm put in front of a done deal, and I have to oppose myself to it, as it goes against the very idea of what we've been planning for months. The solution to this situation, I am afraid, does not lie within my hands. If X is feeling uncomfortable about this, I could understand, but with respect to my in-laws, I just cannot accept this compromise.' So: Am I the asshole? More precisely: Am I the asshole for refusing this, for writing to them clearly that it will not be possible and that they should have contacted me before doing anything? Thanks.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm "the asshole" in this situation. Let me start by understanding the scenario fully. I'm getting married soon, and it's a civil wedding that's supposed to be very intimate. That means only our very close family is invited: parents, siblings, godparents, and their children. The wedding is happening in another country, which adds a layer of complexity because of the different culture and logistics involved. When I sent out the invitations, I was clear about the number of people I was inviting. I invited my parents (2 people) and my godparents' family (4 people). I was also flexible, telling everyone that they could arrive in the country whenever they wanted, as long as they were present for the ceremony. This was because I understood that coordinating travel with four different jobs could be complicated. Additionally, since the destination is far away, my in-laws kindly offered to provide accommodation for everyone. Now, just one month before the wedding, I received a message from my godmother saying that they've booked their flights and that they'll be five people because the godfather of my cousin is joining them. This is where I feel really uncomfortable. It seems like they've made this decision without any prior consultation with me. They didn't even ask if it was okay to have an additional person, someone I've never met. I've always been clear about the number of people I wanted to invite, and I can't stand receiving this kind of "news" via a late evening text message. It's not that I'm against having an additional person. It's just the way I'm being put in front of this decision, as if I had nothing to say. We're not talking about a "party" wedding but something very special meant to be strictly intimate. Moreover, I know that they've had their tickets for a month, and I was waiting for their news to plan the trip, etc. So they literally waited a month to announce this, now that the date is getting closer. I just don't understand this kind of behavior. It costs nothing to make a quick phone call before booking anything and to ask if it's possible, etc. In summary, they just invited someone to my wedding, someone who was never planned and whom I don't even know. This morning, I sent a polite message saying: "I'm confused by your news. I've always been clear about the number of guests and why I picked these specific guests (i.e., you) for our wedding. Why haven't you called me and asked me before booking anything? I'm put in front of a done deal, and I have to oppose myself to it, as it goes against the very idea of what we've been planning for months. The solution to this situation, I am afraid, does not lie within my hands. If X is feeling uncomfortable about this, I could understand, but with respect to my in-laws, I just cannot accept this compromise." So, am I the asshole? More precisely, am I the asshole for refusing this, for writing to them clearly that it will not be possible and that they should have contacted me before doing anything? Alright, now that I've laid out the situation, I need to analyze it step by step to determine whether I'm being unreasonable or if my actions are justified. First, I need to consider the expectations set by me when I sent out the invitations. I was clear about the number of guests and who was invited. I also allowed flexibility in their arrival times but maintained that the number of guests was fixed. This sets a clear expectation that the guest list is final and that any changes should be discussed with me beforehand. Next, I need to think about the communication style used by my godmother. She waited until a month before the wedding to inform me that they were bringing an additional guest. This was done via a text message, which is not the most personal or direct form of communication, especially when discussing something as important as wedding plans. This lack of prior consultation could be seen as disrespectful to my wishes and the effort I've put into planning the event. Furthermore, the additional guest is someone I've never met, which adds another layer of discomfort. Inviting someone I don't know to such an intimate event could make me feel like my preferences and the exclusivity of the event are being overlooked. On the other hand, I need to consider whether my reaction was appropriate. I sent a polite message expressing my confusion and discomfort, but I also made it clear that I was opposed to the additional guest. I emphasized that the solution didn't lie with me, which could be interpreted as shifting responsibility rather than seeking a constructive dialogue. Additionally, I need to reflect on whether there's room for compromise or understanding. Weddings are significant events, and sometimes unexpected situations arise that require flexibility. Perhaps there's a way to accommodate the additional guest without compromising the intimacy of the event, or to have an open conversation about why this change is important to my godmother. I also need to consider cultural differences, as the wedding is taking place in another country. There might be cultural norms or expectations that I'm not fully aware of, which could influence how my godmother approached the situation. Moreover, I should think about the potential impact on my relationship with my godmother and my in-laws. Expressing my discomfort clearly is important, but it's also crucial to maintain respectful communication to preserve these relationships. In summary, while I understand the frustration and discomfort of having the guest list changed without prior consultation, it's essential to approach the situation with empathy and open communication. Perhaps there's a middle ground where both my preferences and my godmother's wishes can be considered. Now, to determine whether I'm "the asshole," I need to assess whether my actions were reasonable and respectful under the circumstances. Did I overreact? Could I have communicated my concerns more effectively? Is there a way to resolve the issue without causing unnecessary tension? Considering all these factors, I believe that while my initial reaction was understandable, there might be a more constructive way to address the issue. Open dialogue, understanding the reasons behind the change, and exploring possible compromises could lead to a resolution that respects both my wishes and those of my godmother.
